title: Asymmetric-horizon continuous-batcher with tiered KV residency and GPU slab compaction
creator: Diego Ramos
description:
Summary: Tuning the continuous batching scheduler to better handle mixed prompt/response length workloads by introducing an asymmetric horizon pacing algorithm, tiered KV residency policies, and GPU slab compaction heuristics. Goal is to reduce p95 generation latency tail and lower per-token GPU memory overhead for long-dialogue workloads without regressing short prompt latency.

Context: Production traffic shows a bimodal length distribution: ~75% short prompts (<64 tokens) and ~25% long-turn dialogues (200-1500 tokens) with heavy KV residency. Current continuous-batcher tends to reserve slots and KV residency for longest-in-flight sequences leading to GPU slab fragmentation, increased eviction churn, and p95 spikes during mixed-load bursts. Existing approaches in repo focus on length-prioritized bins and time-window coalescing, but we see recurring tail regressions when long dialogues interleave with many short requests.

Problem statement: We need a scheduler that: 1) maintains low latency for short requests, 2) avoids unnecessary KV pinning caused by long-turns that block slabs, 3) reclaims GPU slabs deterministically for best-effort long-turns while preserving critical KV for short/high-priority traffic, and 4) keeps throughput stable under bursty interleaved patterns.

Constraints: GPU memory is limited per pod (16-48GB depending on instance), KV cache is shard-local and expensive to rebuild, and we must preserve model correctness (no cross-request KV leakage). Changes must be safe for rollout to Dedicated clusters and opt-in for hosted initially.
updates: 2026-03-02: Baseline perf collected across 5 clusters (eu-west-1, us-west-2) using synthetic interleaved workload (short:long ratio 3:1). Observed p95 increase of 42% during 60s bursts. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/dash/ENG-2398456-baseline

2026-03-04: Spike experiment v1: implemented simple priority-based preemption (short > long) and KV-evict-on-alloc policy. Result: p95 short improved, long-turn throughput regressed by 18%. Added rollback in config. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289

2026-03-06: Design sync with infra and product. Decision to trial two levers together: (1) asymmetric-horizon pacing (time-weighted batching that caps horizon per cohort), (2) tiered-KV (hot/warm/cold residency) with soft eviction and fast-rebuild heuristics. Meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood/company/runtime/ENG-2398456-design

2026-03-09: Prototype commit for tiered-KV and slot-aging logic in scheduler branch eng/ENG-2398456-tiered-kv. Microbenchmarks show 9% GPU memory compaction on average for long-run traces. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1312
2026-03-11: Integration test against smoke harness passed. Preparing canary rollout on dedicated staging pool for A/B run next week.
decisions: Adopt asymmetric-horizon pacing: limit batching horizon per priority cohort (short/interactive vs long/background) and compute dynamic coalescing thresholds based on recent latency percentiles.

Use tiered KV residency: hot (pinned for interactive), warm (soft-pinned with fast rebuild hint), cold (evictable). Residency promotion/demotion driven by recency and explicit priority tags from API (priority header).
Introduce GPU slab compaction pass that triggers on CV RAM fragmentation above 70% and during low-utilization windows to defragment and reduce evictions for hot KV entries.
Make new scheduler toggles feature-flagged and opt-in per deployment; default off for hosted until canary validates metrics.
Avoid global preemption; prefer soft-preemption where long-turn batches are deprioritized but allowed to progress using spare capacity to preserve throughput.
Instrument detailed metrics for KV hit-rate, slab-fragmentation, slot-age distributions, and per-cohort p50/p95 latencies; expose these in Console rollout UI.
acceptance_criteria: Canary run (48h) shows no regression >3% in p50 short-request latency and reduces p95 short latency by >=12% compared to baseline.
KV cold rebuild rate does not exceed baseline by more than 10% and average rebuild time < 120ms.
Overall GPU memory compaction reduces fragmentation metric (fragmentation_index) by >=15% in mixed workloads.
Throughput for long-turn cohort remains within 15% of baseline when averaged across 24h period.
No customer-facing errors attributable to KV eviction or cross-request contamination.
test_plan: Unit tests for slot-aging, tier promotion/demotion, and slab compaction heuristics.
Load tests with synthetic mixed distributions: short-heavy (3:1), balanced (1:1), and long-heavy (1:3) using existing harness in infra/testing/batcher-harness.
Fault injection: simulate KV shard eviction and slow rebuild to confirm soft-degradation and fallback policies.
Canary A/B: Rollout to 10% of dedicated-staging cluster and compare against control for 48 hours with automated guards. If any safety guard trips, auto-rollback.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): Implement asymmetric-horizon pacing and metrics wiring. Feature-flag off. (PRs: runtime#1298, scheduler#44)
Phase 2 (week 2): Add tiered KV residency and slot-aging with soft eviction; integrate compact pass. Start microbenchmarks. (PR runtime#1312)
Phase 3 (week 3): Canary rollout and iteratively tune thresholds (horizon caps, warm residency timeouts, compaction trigger). Dashboarding and alert thresholds.
Phase 4: Rollout to hosted if canary meets acceptance criteria, then schedule Dedicated opt-in and enablement docs for customers.
